description: Project foundation: folder layout, display settings, input map, and a CLAUDE.md with conventions so later iterations stay consistent.
steps: Create the folder structure exactly as drawn in the '# Folder Structure' section of project_plan.txt (add a .gitkeep to empty folders). Every later feature must put its files in the folders that section describes.

In project.godot set display/window/size/viewport_width=1920, viewport_height=1080, display/window/stretch/mode="canvas_items", display/window/stretch/aspect="expand" (target is Windows now, maybe iPad later).

Add input actions: move_up/move_down/move_left/move_right (WASD + arrow keys + gamepad left stick), interact (E, Space, gamepad A), menu (Esc, gamepad Start), confirm (Enter, Space), cancel (Esc, Backspace).

Write CLAUDE.md: Godot 4.7, typed GDScript. Keep every image a placeholder (see PlaceholderBox) sized/positioned where real art will go. Code style: (1) prefer composition over inheritance: build behaviour from small reusable component nodes/Resources (e.g. HealthComponent, StatsComponent, SkillSetComponent, InteractionComponent) attached as children, not deep class hierarchies; extend only Godot built-ins plus at most one thin project base class. (2) Structure files per the '# Folder Structure' section of project_plan.txt: copy that tree into CLAUDE.md, and keep a scene's script next to its .tscn with the same name.
Add .claude_output.txt to .gitignore (ralph.sh temp file).
Verify: if godot_console is on PATH, run `godot_console --headless --path . --import` and fix any errors it prints.
notes: Done 2026-10-31. Folders + .gitkeep, _production_files/.gdignore, display + input map in project.godot, CLAUDE.md, .gitignore. Headless Godot check run by the user with Godot 4.7.2: no errors or warnings.

description: Reusable placeholder visuals: white box with gray border that stretches to any size, plus a shared UI theme.
steps: Create PlaceholderBox (PanelContainer or Panel) using a StyleBoxFlat: white fill, 2-4px gray border. Export a `label_text` string drawn centered in gray (e.g. 'HERO PORTRAIT') so it is obvious what art goes there.
Create ui/common/ui_theme.tres with simple black/white/gray styling for Button, Label, LineEdit, ProgressBar, TabBar, ItemList, and set it as the project default theme (gui/theme/custom).
Use only these placeholders for art in every later feature.
notes: Done 2026-10-31. PlaceholderBox is a Panel (not PanelContainer) so long labels cannot grow the box; set a size or custom_minimum_size when using it, because its minimum size is 0. Theme also styles Panel and PanelContainer, and the default clear color is now white, so black theme text stays readable. Import clean; default-state rendering checked with a screenshot. Hover, pressed and focus states not checked visually.

description: Global singletons: GameState (party, gold, xp, overworld position), SceneRouter (scene switching by name), AudioManager (stub music/sfx calls).
steps: Create components/health/health_component.gd (max_hp, hp, damage(), heal(), signals hp_changed/died) and components/combat_stats/stats_component.gd (speed etc.). Heroes in GameState hold plain data; scenes that show a unit attach these components rather than subclassing.

GameState: `party: Array` of 3 hero dictionaries or a Hero Resource {name, class_id, start_slot (1-3), current_slot, primary_weapon_slot (= start_slot), unlocked_weapon_slots, max_hp, hp, speed, equipment{}}, plus gold:int, xp:int, xp_to_next:int, overworld_position:Vector2, inventory:Array (36 slots). Add `reset()` and `to_dict()/from_dict()` for saving.
SceneRouter: `go_to(name: String)` mapping names (main_menu, load_game, party_create, overworld, combat) to scene paths, using change_scene_to_file. Add a short fade if easy, otherwise plain switch.
AudioManager: `play_music(id)` and `play_sfx(id)` that play a file from assets/audio/music/ or assets/audio/sfx/ if it exists and silently do nothing otherwise.
Register all three as autoloads in project.godot.
notes: Done 2026-10-31. GameState heroes are dictionaries built by GameState.make_hero(). SceneRouter fades 0.2s to black and reports unknown names or missing scene files with push_error; only the placeholder_box test scene has been switched to so far, because the five real scenes do not exist yet. AudioManager checks .ogg, .mp3, .wav in that order and always loops music. Import clean; 26 throwaway behaviour checks pass. Open: Godot reports 4 leaked instances at exit if audio is playing when the game quits (seen headless only); recheck when main-menu-01 adds music and Quit.

description: First-pass game data for hero classes (Fighter, Mage, Priest) and one enemy (Muck Ball), including slot-based skill names so UI has something real to show.
steps: classes.gd: a const Dictionary for fighter, mage, priest: display name, base max_hp, speed, starting weapon id, class_skill (always available), class_slot_skills {1,2,3} with a one-line description each, and a short 'best slot' blurb for the party-creation screen.
weapons.gd: one starter weapon per class (e.g. sword, staff, mace) each with default_ability and abilities for slots 1, 2, 3 (name, damage/heal number, target rule like 'enemy slot 4-5').
enemies.gd: muck_ball: size 'sm' (1 slot), max_hp, speed, one attack. Leave room for md/lg/xl sizes (slot_span field).
Numbers are placeholders; keep them simple.
Put each data file in its resources/ subfolder (see '# Folder Structure' in project_plan.txt).

description: SaveManager: save/load/list games as JSON in user://saves/.
steps: save_game(save_name) writes GameState.to_dict() plus save_name and timestamp to user://saves/<sanitized_name>.json.
list_saves() returns [{save_name, timestamp, path}] newest first; has_saves() -> bool.
load_game(path) reads JSON and calls GameState.from_dict(). autosave() saves to a fixed 'autosave' slot.
Register as autoload.

description: Main menu: background image + title placeholders, centered vertical buttons, music, set as the project's main scene.
steps: Full-screen PlaceholderBox background ('BACKGROUND ART') and a title label/placeholder near the top.
Centered vertical VBox: Continue / Load Game (hidden or disabled when SaveManager.has_saves() is false), New Game, Quit.
New Game -> SceneRouter.go_to('party_create'); Load Game -> 'load_game'; Quit -> get_tree().quit().
Call AudioManager.play_music('main_menu'). Set run/main_scene to this scene.

description: Load game screen: scrolling list of saves, Back button lower left.
steps: ScrollContainer with one row per save (name + date). Show 'No saved games' when empty.
Clicking a row loads it via SaveManager then SceneRouter.go_to('overworld').
Back button anchored lower-left returns to main menu; cancel action does the same.

description: Create Party screen: 3 hero columns (slot 1 to 3, left to right) with class cycling, name entry and a slot explanation; Back lower left, Begin lower right.
steps: Make a reusable HeroSlotPanel: slot label ('Slot 1 - Back' ... 'Slot 3 - Front'), portrait PlaceholderBox, < class name > buttons cycling Fighter/Mage/Priest, LineEdit for name (max 9 chars), and an info box showing the class skill, the class slot skill for THIS slot, and the weapon skill for this slot.
Note in the panel that this slot becomes the hero's primary weapon slot.
Begin button lower-right is enabled only when all 3 names are 3-9 characters (plan says > 2 and < 10).

On Begin: GameState.reset(), fill the 3 heroes (start_slot/current_slot/primary_weapon_slot = their column, unlocked_weapon_slots = [that slot], starting weapon equipped there, hp = max_hp), then go to overworld.
Back button lower-left returns to main menu.

description: Overworld scene with a placeholder map and a player that moves freely in any direction (not grid-locked).
steps: Build a simple map large enough to scroll (e.g. 3000x3000) out of placeholder ground areas (grass/forest look-alikes can just be differently labeled boxes or ColorRects) and a few StaticBody2D obstacles plus map-edge walls.
Player: CharacterBody2D with PlaceholderBox sprite (~48x64), Input.get_vector for analog any-angle movement, move_and_slide, and a `facing: Vector2` updated from last non-zero input.
Camera2D follows the player with limits set to the map bounds.
On ready, place the player at GameState.overworld_position if set; keep it updated while moving.

description: Overworld HUD: Menu button top-left, wide XP bar at the bottom, 3 hero portraits with HP bars/status icons above XP bar on the left, gold on the right.
steps: CanvasLayer HUD. Menu button top-left (opens escape menu once it exists; emit a signal for now).
ProgressBar XP bar along the bottom, ~95% screen width, driven by GameState.xp / xp_to_next.
Reusable HeroStatusWidget: HP bar + a row of small status icon placeholders above a portrait PlaceholderBox and name. Reuse this in combat later.
Gold label bottom-right above the XP bar. HUD refreshes from GameState.

description: Interact with things in front of the player and a basic dialogue box (read text, press a button to advance).
steps: Make components/interaction/interactable_component.gd: a child node that marks its parent as interactable and holds what happens on interact. Player gets an InteractionComponent (RayCast2D/Area2D along `facing`) that calls it when interact is pressed.
NPC scene (PlaceholderBox) exporting `lines: Array[String]` and an optional speaker name; place one NPC on the map.
DialogueBox on a CanvasLayer at the bottom of the screen: speaker name, text, '▼' prompt; confirm/interact advances, closes after last line. Player movement is disabled while it is open.
Expose a simple `DialogueBox.show_lines(lines)` so story scripts can use it later.

description: Random encounters based on zone/terrain the player stands on, transitioning to combat and back.
steps: EncounterZone: Area2D exporting zone name, encounter_rate, and an enemy table (e.g. [['muck_ball'], ['muck_ball','muck_ball']]). Place 2 zones with different rates; a safe area with none.
Track distance walked; every N pixels roll against the current zone's rate.
On encounter: save overworld_position, store chosen enemy group in GameState.pending_encounter, go to combat.
After combat, overworld restores the player position. Add a short no-encounter grace period after returning.

description: Combat screen layout (Darkest Dungeon style side view): battle area top 2/3, action panel bottom 1/3, turn queue top-left.
steps: Top 2/3: 3 hero slot markers on the left (slot 1 far left/back, slot 3 nearest centre/front) and 4 enemy slot markers on the right (slot 4 nearest centre/front, slot 7 far right/back). Heroes face right, enemies face left.
Units are PlaceholderBox figures; an enemy's width spans 1-4 slots by size (sm/md/lg/xl). HeroStatusWidget-style HP bar and status icons under each unit.
Turn queue strip top-left: small portrait placeholders, current unit leftmost.

Bottom 1/3 two columns. Left: selected hero portrait + name and buttons: Weapon Skill, Weapon Slot Skill, Class Skill, Class Slot Skill, Trinket 1, Trinket 2, Item 1, Item 2, Move (shows cooldown), Pass. Unavailable buttons are disabled. Right: info panel for whatever unit is hovered.
Build from GameState.party and GameState.pending_encounter (fallback: one muck_ball for testing when run directly).
Combat units are one CombatUnit scene composed of HealthComponent + StatsComponent + SkillSetComponent children, configured from hero or enemy data. Do NOT make Hero/Enemy subclasses.

description: Minimal working turn loop: initiative, choose skill + target, enemy turns, win/lose.
steps: Initiative: each unit rolls speed + randi_range(0, N); sort descending to fill the turn queue; rebuild each round.

SkillSetComponent resolves skills by current slot: weapon skill = default ability of weapon in the weapon slot matching current_slot, else primary weapon slot; weapon slot skill = that weapon's ability for current_slot; class skill and class slot skill from data. Labels update when the hero moves.
Hero turn: pick skill, click a valid target (highlight valid targets), apply placeholder damage/heal, advance queue.
Move: swap with an adjacent hero, does not end the turn, then goes on cooldown. Pass: hero is pushed back a random number of places in the queue.
Enemy turn: Muck Ball attacks a random living hero (slightly favour front slots).
Win: grant xp/gold to GameState, return to overworld. All heroes dead: simple 'Defeated' message then main menu.

description: Escape menu overlay: Inventory / Status / Quest tabs top-left, Save and Exit buttons top-right; pauses the overworld.
steps: Opened by the 'menu' action or the HUD Menu button; pauses the tree (menu uses process_mode ALWAYS); Esc closes it.
Tabs top-left: Inventory, Status, Quest. Status and Quest just show a 'Coming soon' label (out of scope).
Top-right Save button opens a small save panel: LineEdit for save name + Save button calling SaveManager.save_game; show 'Saved'.
Top-right Exit button calls SaveManager.autosave() then returns to the main menu (unpause first).

description: Inventory tab layout with hero tabs, ragdoll + stats, equipment slots, 6x6 grid and hover/selected compare panels.
steps: Left half: 3 hero tabs on top. Below, sub-column 1 = ragdoll PlaceholderBox with stats list under it; sub-column 2 = equip slots: Weapon 1/2/3, Head, Necklace, Ring 1, Body, Ring 2, Trinket 1, Boots, Trinket 2, Combat Item 1, Combat Item 2. Locked weapon slots look locked (only unlocked_weapon_slots usable).
Right half: 'Sort' dropdown above a 6x6 grid of reusable ItemSlot buttons. Seed GameState.inventory with 2-3 dummy items for testing.
Below the grid: left panel shows info for the hovered item, right panel for the clicked (selected) item.
Equipping/drag-drop is NOT required yet; layout and hover/select info only.

description: End-to-end pass of the shell game: everything connects and nothing errors.
steps: Trace the flow in code: main menu -> new game -> party create -> overworld -> talk to NPC -> random encounter -> combat win -> overworld -> escape menu -> save -> exit -> main menu -> load game -> overworld.
If godot_console is on PATH, run `godot_console --headless --path . --import` and fix all script/scene errors.
Fix broken scene paths, missing autoload references and signal hookups. Record anything that needs a human to test by hand in ralph_progress.txt.
Check code style: every file sits where the '# Folder Structure' section of project_plan.txt says, and no inheritance chains where a component would do.
